name: Kimi-K2
notes: The largest open-weight MoE at its release and the first to exceed 1T total. Vendor: 1T total / 32B activated; safetensors total 1026.41B; our config arithmetic gives 1026.2B / 32.7B, matching to ~2%. The brief's '1T' is confirmed and then some. kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 61 layers x (kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64) x 2 bytes = 61 x 576 x 2 = 70,272 B/token (68.6 KiB) - identical to DeepSeek-V3, because K2 is DeepSeek-V3-shaped: same 61 layers, same MLA geometry, same hidden 7168. It is V3 scaled in experts, not in depth: 384 routed + 1 shared (V3's 256), 8 per token, but first_k_dense_replace 1 instead of 3, and num_key_value_heads 64 instead of 128. qk_nope_head_dim 128, qk_rope_head_dim 64, v_head_dim 128, q_lora_rank 1536 - all identical to V3. Context: max_position_embeddings 131072 via YaRN factor 32 over an original 4096, rope_theta 50000 (V3 uses 10000) with beta_fast 1.0 / beta_slow 1.0 (V3 uses 32 / 1) - a gentler, more uniform RoPE adjustment. Trained with the Muon optimizer, which is the notable difference from V3 rather than an architectural one. num_nextn_predict_layers 0 - no MTP. Licence is a 'Modified MIT License' (Moonshot, 2025) - commercially usable but with vendor-specific clauses; not plain MIT. Kimi-K2-Thinking is the same config with a different serving mode.
